To activate an activated ability, announce it, choose any targets and modes, and pay its costs. It then goes on the stack. [CR 701.2]
Activating its {T} ability taps it to add {G}.

To attach an Aura, Equipment or Fortification to an object or player is to move it onto that object or player. It can't be attached to something it couldn't enchant, equip or fortify; if it can't, it doesn't move. Re-attaching to what it's already attached to does nothing. Attaching gives it a new timestamp. [CR 701.3]
Equip attaches it to a creature you control.
To cast a spell is to take it from where it is (usually your hand), put it on the stack, choose modes and targets, and pay its costs. [CR 701.5]
Cast it for {R}, then it's on the stack until it resolves.

To counter a spell or ability is to remove it from the stack so it doesn't resolve and none of its effects occur. A countered spell goes to its owner's graveyard. Costs already paid aren't refunded. (Not the same as a counter placed on a permanent.) [CR 701.6]
To create a token is to put it onto the battlefield. [CR 701.7]
Creates two 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens.
To destroy a permanent is to move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard. Regeneration and indestructible can stop it. [CR 701.8]
To discard a card is to put it from your hand into your graveyard. [CR 701.9]

To double a creature's power or toughness, give it +X/+0 or +0/+X where X is the current value. To double life, gain or lose life so the new total is twice the old one. To double counters or mana, add as many as you already have. Doubling damage is a replacement effect. [CR 701.10]
Doubles the power of target creature.

To exchange control, life totals, or other things is to swap them. If the whole exchange can't be completed, none of it happens. Exchanging control of two permanents controlled by the same player does nothing. [CR 701.12]
To exile an object is to put it into the exile zone from wherever it was. [CR 701.13]

Each of two creatures deals damage equal to its power to the other. If either is no longer a creature on the battlefield (or is an illegal target), neither deals damage. A creature fighting itself deals twice its power to itself. Fight damage isn't combat damage. [CR 701.14]
Target creature you control fights target creature you don't control.
To mill a number of cards is to put that many cards from the top of a library into its owner's graveyard. [CR 701.17]

To play a land is to put it onto the battlefield as a special action (your turn, main phase, empty stack, land drop available). To play a card is to play it as a land or cast it as a spell. Putting a land onto the battlefield with an effect isn't playing it. [CR 701.18]
You can play the land you reveal.

Regeneration creates a shield. The next time the permanent would be destroyed this turn, instead remove all damage from it, tap it, and remove it from combat. Effects saying it 'can't be regenerated' stop the shield from applying. [CR 701.19]
To reveal a card is to show it to all players for a brief time. [CR 701.20]
Search your library for four cards and reveal them; an opponent chooses two to go to your hand.
To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard. You can sacrifice only permanents you control. Indestructible doesn't help. [CR 701.21]

Scry N: look at the top N cards of your library, then put any number on the bottom in any order and the rest on top in any order. Scry 0 does nothing and doesn't trigger 'whenever you scry'. [CR 701.22]

To search a zone for a card, look through it for a card matching the description. When searching a hidden zone for a stated quality (a card type, color...) you aren't required to find a match, even if one is there. Shuffling is part of the effect that says so, not part of searching. [CR 701.23]
Search your library for a basic land.
To shuffle a library is to randomize the cards in it. [CR 701.24]
Sacrifice it to search for a basic land, then shuffle.
To tap a permanent is to turn it sideways; only untapped permanents can be tapped. To untap is to turn it back upright; only tapped permanents can be untapped. [CR 701.26]
Taps target artifact, creature or land.

Each player, starting with a specified player and going in turn order, chooses one of the available options. 'Voting' refers only to effects that actually say 'vote'. An effect that gives a player extra votes has those votes happen at the same time. [CR 701.38]
Bolster N: choose a creature with the least toughness among creatures you control and put N +1/+1 counters on it. [CR 701.39]
Put the top card of your library onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature. If it's a creature card, you can turn it face up for its mana cost. [CR 701.40]
Manifests the top card of your library.
Support N on a permanent: put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to N other target creatures. On an instant or sorcery, it's 'up to N target creatures' (not limited to 'other'). [CR 701.41]
Create a Clue token: an artifact with '{2}, Sacrifice this artifact: Draw a card.' [CR 701.16]
Put two cards that form a meld pair onto the battlefield back faces up, combined as one permanent. Tokens and non-pair cards can't be melded; if they can't, they stay where they are. [CR 701.42]
Melds with Bruna, the Fading Light.

Until your next turn, the goaded creature attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than you if able. A creature can be goaded by several players at once; goading it again by the same player does nothing. Goaded is a designation, not an ability. [CR 701.15]
Goads all creatures your opponents control.
You may exert a creature as it attacks. It won't untap during your next untap step. [CR 701.43]
Exert for 4 damage to a non-Dragon creature.
Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a land, put it into your hand. Otherwise put a +1/+1 counter on this creature, then you may put the card into your graveyard. [CR 701.44]
Surveil N: look at the top N cards of your library, then put any number into your graveyard and the rest on top in any order. [CR 701.25]
Adapt N: if this creature has no +1/+1 counters on it, put N +1/+1 counters on it. [CR 701.46]

Amass [subtype] N: if you don't control an Army creature, create a 0/0 black Army token of that subtype (older cards say Zombie). Then choose an Army you control and put N +1/+1 counters on it. It becomes that subtype in addition to its other types. [CR 701.47]
You may discard a card; if you do, draw a card. If you didn't discard a card, you may reveal a Lesson card you own from outside the game and put it into your hand. [CR 701.48]

Draw a card, then discard a card. If you discarded a nonland card, put a +1/+1 counter on the conniving creature. 'Connive N' draws N, discards N, and adds a counter for each nonland card discarded. [CR 701.50]
Move your venture marker to the next room in a dungeon, starting a new one if needed, and get the room's effect. [CR 701.49]
Ventures into the dungeon when it enters or attacks.

Choose any number of permanents and/or players that have a counter, then give each one additional counter of each kind it already has. (In Two-Headed Giant, a team's poison counters are shared, so only one teammate gets one.) [CR 701.34]
Proliferates when you cast noncreature spells.
Turn a double-faced permanent over to its other face. [CR 701.27]
Transforms into Insectile Aberration, a 3/2 flier.
Fateseal N: look at the top N cards of an opponent's library, then put any number on the bottom and the rest on top. [CR 701.29]
Fateseal 2: look at the top two cards of an opponent's library and bottom any you want them not to draw.

You and an opponent each reveal the top card of your library, then each may put that card on the bottom. A player wins the clash if they revealed a card with a higher mana value than all the other revealed cards. [CR 701.30]
You and an opponent each reveal your top card. The player with the higher mana value wins the clash and gets a bonus effect.
Used in Planechase: put each face-up plane or phenomenon on the bottom of the planar deck and turn the top card of the planar deck face up. Only the planar controller can planeswalk. [CR 701.31]
In Planechase, rolling the planeswalker symbol makes you planeswalk to a new plane.
Create a token that's a copy of a creature token you control. [CR 701.36]
Populate, then creatures you control gain indestructible. Populate copies a creature token you control.
Until your next turn, the detained permanent can't attack or block and its activated abilities can't be activated. [CR 701.35]
When it enters, detain a creature an opponent controls: until your next turn it can't attack or block.
Monstrosity N: if this creature isn't monstrous, put N +1/+1 counters on it and it becomes monstrous. [CR 701.37]
Monstrosity 4: pay the cost once to put four +1/+1 counters on it, making a 8/9 reach creature.
For each suspended card you own and each permanent you control with a time counter, you may add or remove a time counter. [CR 701.56]
Add or remove a time counter from each suspended card and each permanent you control that has time counters.

Choose a creature you control as your Ring-bearer. You get The Ring emblem the first time: your Ring-bearer is legendary and can't be blocked by creatures with greater power. Each further temptation unlocks a stronger ability (loot on attack, sacrifice the blocker, then 3 life loss on combat damage). [CR 701.54]
At the beginning of your upkeep, the Ring tempts you, choosing or confirming your Ring-bearer.
Create an Incubator token with N +1/+1 counters and '{2}: Transform this artifact'. It becomes a 0/0 Phyrexian creature. [CR 701.53]
Create an Incubator token with N +1/+1 counters. Pay {2} to transform it into a Phyrexian creature of that size.
Exile three cards from your graveyard or sacrifice a Food. [CR 701.61]
Pay the forage cost by exiling three cards from your graveyard or sacrificing a Food.
Exile cards from your graveyard with total mana value N or greater. [CR 701.59]
A suspected creature has menace and can't block. [CR 701.60]
A suspected creature has menace and can't block until it stops being suspected.
Put the top card of your library onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. [CR 701.58]
Puts the top card of your library onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 with ward {2}. If it's a creature card you may turn it face up by paying its mana cost.
Look at the top two cards of your library. Manifest one and put the other into your graveyard. [CR 701.62]
Look at the top two cards of your library. Manifest one as a face-down 2/2 and put the other in your graveyard.
Endure N: put N +1/+1 counters on this permanent, or create an N/N white Spirit creature token. Endure 0 does nothing. [CR 701.63]
Endure 2: put two +1/+1 counters on the creature, or create a 2/2 white Spirit token.

Discover N: exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card with mana value N or less. Cast it for free (if its mana value is N or less), or put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom in a random order. [CR 701.57]

'Behold a [quality]' means reveal a [quality] card from your hand or choose a [quality] permanent you control on the battlefield. 'If a [quality] was beheld' checks whether the object had that quality when you did it. [CR 701.4]
To behold an Elf, you may reveal an Elf card from your hand or point at an Elf you control.
Like double, but three times as much. Tripling power gives +X/+0 where X is twice the creature's current power (so it ends at three times its power); same for toughness. [CR 701.11]
A 3/2 creature has its power tripled: it gets +6/+0 and becomes 9/2.
To convert a permanent is to turn it so its other face is up. It follows the same rules as transform, but they're different actions. If it can't transform, it also can't convert. [CR 701.28]
A permanent with a robot face and a vehicle face converts to its other face; a 'whenever this transforms' trigger doesn't care, but 'transforms into' triggers do.
Archenemy only. To set a scheme in motion, move the top card of your scheme deck off the deck and turn it face up. Only the archenemy does this, one scheme at a time. [CR 701.32]
At the start of your precombat main phase as the archenemy, you set a scheme in motion.
Archenemy only. To abandon a face-up ongoing scheme, turn it face down and put it on the bottom of its owner's scheme deck. [CR 701.33]
An ongoing scheme tells you to abandon it; it goes face down on the bottom of your scheme deck.
A keyword action from the silver-bordered Unstable set that puts Contraptions onto the battlefield. The Comprehensive Rules don't cover Unstable mechanics. [CR 701.45]
Move the top card of your Attraction deck, turn it face up, and put it onto the battlefield under your control. Only works if you're playing with an Attraction deck. [CR 701.51]
An effect says to open an Attraction: you put the top Attraction card from your Attraction deck onto the battlefield.
Roll a six-sided die. Each Attraction you control with that number lit up has been visited, so its visit ability triggers. [CR 701.52]
You roll a 4; every Attraction you control with 4 lit up is visited.

The player chooses one of two options given and performs it. They may choose an option that is illegal or impossible and do as much of it as possible. If several players face the choice, they do so one at a time in APNAP order. [CR 701.55]
An effect says an opponent faces a villainous choice: they choose to either sacrifice a creature or lose 4 life, and carry out the choice.

'Harness [this permanent]': if it isn't harnessed, it becomes harnessed. Harnessed is a designation that lasts until the permanent leaves the battlefield. It matters for the Infinity (∞) ability. [CR 701.64]
You harness a permanent; now its ∞ abilities are active.
Exile the chosen permanents and/or spells. For as long as each remains exiled, its owner may cast it by paying {2} instead of its mana cost. [CR 701.65]
You airbend a creature: it's exiled, and its owner can recast it from exile for {2}.

Earthbend N: target land you control becomes a 0/0 land creature with haste in addition to its other types, and gets N +1/+1 counters. When it dies or is put into exile, return it to the battlefield tapped under your control. [CR 701.66]
You earthbend 3 a Forest: it becomes a 3/3 haste creature land, and if it dies you get it back tapped.

Waterbend [cost]: pay the cost, but for each generic mana in it you may tap an untapped artifact or creature you control instead. This only applies to the generic mana in the waterbend cost itself. [CR 701.67]
Its additional cost is waterbend {6}: tap up to six artifacts and/or creatures, but you can't tap them to pay for its {1}{U}{U} mana cost.
Blight N: put N -1/-1 counters on a creature you control. If you control no creature you can't choose to blight. Effects may refer to 'the blighted creature'. [CR 701.68]
You blight 2: put two -1/-1 counters on one creature you control.
To heal damage already dealt to a permanent, remove that marked damage from it. If damage 'is healed', its controller removes all marked damage from it. [CR 701.69]
A creature has taken 3 damage; healing it removes all 3 marked damage.
Draw a card, then discard a card. If you discarded a nonland card this way, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token. [CR 701.70]
You recruit and discard a creature card, so you create a 1/1 Human Soldier.

Empower Jace N: if you don't control a Jace planeswalker token, create a blue Jace planeswalker token with 0 loyalty, '[-1]: Surveil 1,' and '[-3]: Draw a card.' Then choose a Jace planeswalker token you control and put N loyalty counters on it. [CR 701.71]
You empower Jace 3 with no Jace token: create the token, then put 3 loyalty counters on it.
